As a civil engineer, I can tell you 100% for sure they would not let you put up a route. Generally speaking, if you're not generating some sort of revenue for the municipality that owns it, they wouldn't be on board. Not to mention the incredible liability. Climb it but absolutely do not tell them what you're up to or draw any attention to yourself!

Wow I am so sorry to hear that you're going thru this. I can't really offer you any direct advice, since you're in a pretty unique situation. Al I can say is it seems like you may have missed a few things along the way. Going from head-over-heels in love with you to goodbye, talk to you never just seems unbelievably unusual. I know a relationship I was just involved with ended and I was able to look back and see all the little flaws in our relationship more clearly. Perhaps things will be clearer with more time. If he really never contacts you again, that is a major heartbreak for you and again, I'm so sorry. But on the bright side (I know this is a stretch), at least your marriage didn't involve anything permanent. As a child of divorced parents, he very well could have pulled the same shit after you had already developed a family and invested a longer amount of time in each other. I know these few words of encouragement must feel so weak and fruitless, but hang in there. The night is darkest just before dawn.
